open_decisions.question: DB2ERR (line 75) uses the non-standard 'ACCEPT WS-CURRENT-TIMESTAMP FROM TIME STAMP'; the ERRPROC logic file flags the same construct (line 57) and PORTDEL uses it for the deletion audit timestamp (source line 169). Which compiler extension is in use and what timestamp format do ERRLOG rows, error-log records and deletion audit records actually carry?

Error paths do not stop as expected: PORTADD and PORTDEL continue the read loop on closed files after an open failure (returning RC 8), and PORTMSTR's 9000-ERROR GOBACKs from inside a PERFORM after closing a possibly unopened file. Should Java reproduce this behaviour or end the step/call immediately with RC 8?

PORTADD and PORTDEL (key PORT-KEY, PORTFLIO layout) and PORTMSTR (key PORT-ID, 103-byte PORTFOLIO-RECORD) all ASSIGN TO PORTFILE as an indexed file. Do they address the same VSAM dataset, and if so which record layout and key are authoritative?

Which character encoding (code page) do the files and areas described by these copybooks use for DISPLAY data on the legacy platform (EBCDIC 037, 1140, another EBCDIC variant, or ASCII)? The zoned-decimal test vectors and String codecs depend on it.

On an open failure PORTDEL sets return code 8 and 3000-TERMINATE returns (line 126); 0000-MAIN still runs 2000-PROCESS on closed files and 3000-TERMINATE again, and whether the loop ends depends on run-time file status, so deletion counts and audit writes are unpredictable. Should the batch delete stop immediately after an open failure?

The deletion request declares reason codes '01' account closed, '02' transferred and '03' client requested, and the code is copied into the deletion audit record, but it is not validated before the portfolio is deleted. Should the modern system validate the reason code (and reject or count requests with other values) or keep accepting any value?

Which portfolio status domain is authoritative? PORTMSTR validates 'A', 'I', 'C' (VALID-STATUS, BR-095) while copybook PORTFLIO used by PORTADD and PORTDEL declares 'A' active, 'C' closed, 'S' suspended (BR-149); 'I' and 'S' each exist in only one place, and the PORTFLIO and PORTMSTR records are linked only by naming convention (REL-002, GAP-091). What do 'I' and 'S' mean, and do PORTMSTR and the batch programs maintain the same portfolio master?
